title: AISF members detained at Itarsi while travelling to Delhi protest
seoTitle: Itarsi AISF members detained en route to Delhi

tea.why: Students and activists travelled to demand the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner over electoral roll revisions.
tea.want: To participate in a demonstration in New Delhi demanding the resignation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
tea.changed: Oct 9: Madhya Pradesh High Court issued notices to authorities and ordered them to produce the detained students by October 13.

summary: Students travelling from Pune to New Delhi aboard the Goa Express were intercepted and taken off their train by Government Railway Police at Itarsi Junction in Madhya Pradesh. The travellers, identified as members of the All India Students’ Federation, were heading to participate in a demonstration called by the Cockroach Janta Party to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in electoral roll revisions. Organisers claimed activists were manhandled and their whereabouts initially concealed, while police stated the detentions were executed under lawful directions and orders from above because the travellers lacked permission. A GRP inspector later claimed the students were released and staying at a hotel voluntarily, though reports indicated they remained restricted inside a banquet hall. The Madhya Pradesh High Court subsequently issued notices to the state and police following a habeas corpus petition.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
response: Police stated they detained the individuals following orders from above because they lacked permission to join the protest. A GRP inspector claimed they were later released and staying at a hotel voluntarily, though police also noted they refused to leave the private hotel.

injuries.text: a woman even injured and bruised her leg

updates.text: Police intercepted AISF members on the Goa Express at Itarsi railway station and detained them.
Police claimed the detained students were released but refused to leave the private hotel.
The Madhya Pradesh High Court issued notices to authorities and asked them to produce the students by October 13.
